findings.checklist_item: Specify which deletion commit to honor when a path is deleted more than once in tickets history (e.g. NEWEST deletion, opposite of the oldest-add overwrite in build_ticket_position_commit_map) so the blob read at its parent is the correct/final content.
evidence: authorship.py:374 comment: 'newest->oldest walk; overwrite so the OLDEST add wins'
AC1: 'enumerated by ONE ticket-scoped git log --diff-filter=D --name-only pass modelled on build_ticket_position_commit_map, each blob read at the deleting commit's parent'
for a path deleted, re-added, and deleted again, oldest-deletion parent ≠ the parent holding the last-written content
findings.finding: AC1/AC4 mandate the deletion walk be 'modelled on build_ticket_position_commit_map', but that helper streams commits newest->oldest and OVERWRITES so the OLDEST entry wins (authorship.py:374). That is correct for --diff-filter=A (oldest ADD introduces the event), but for --diff-filter=D on a path added/deleted more than once it selects the OLDEST deletion, whose parent may not hold the intended (final) blob content; the plan does not specify which deletion commit to honor.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria, AC1 ('each blob read at the deleting commit's parent') and AC4
scenarios: A ticket path that was compacted-deleted, restored, and compacted-deleted a second time in tickets history — the oldest-deletion parent yields a stale earlier version of that event file

findings.finding: AC4 does not resolve the flag choices the analogous authorship.py walks document as load-bearing — most notably `--full-history` (needed to see a compacted event whose delete/add commit is off the first-parent chain), plus `--no-renames`, `--no-merges`, and `-c log.showSignature=false`; leaving these unstated risks the deletion scan silently missing exactly the compacted files it must recover.

b636 comment: the 'pre-a3-remediation' tag 'is NOT a safe rollback point ... the clean baseline is bba514cd3318...', so rollback safety is load-bearing and known-fragile.

DATA LOSS RISK: no AC asserts on the state AFTER a rebuild that produces a wrong result, nor names a back-out path for the in-place snapshot rewrite across the population; the held-out tests cover only the single close-restored ticket and the refuse case.
findings.finding: The plan performs an in-place, one-way rewrite of SNAPSHOT records during rebuild but asserts no back-out path and does not assert on post-rebuild state — it only requires the held-out ticket 'reads closed again', with no check that the restore+rebuild did not mis-derive status for other tickets in the 505 population and no safe rollback point.

scenarios: restore+rebuild derives an incorrect status for some subset of the 505 tickets and there is no back-out to a known-good store state
an operator needs to revert a bad repair run but the only tag points mid-run

findings.checklist_item: State that restore_deleted_sources and rebuild_with_restore are idempotent and resumable — re-writing an already-restored `.retired` source and re-running the rebuild are no-ops (mirroring compaction's existing `.retired`-exists skip at compact.py:337-338).
evidence: The AC writes each recovered blob 'back as a folded `.retired` source (never resurrected as a live event)' but no AC asserts re-runnability.

The existing compaction fold is explicitly idempotent — compact.py:337-338 skips an existing `.retired` target on re-run — so the resumability contract exists in prior art but the plan does not carry it over.
ABSENCE: at 505-ticket scale a partial/interrupted repair run is likely, and no AC states whether a second `fsck --repair` double-writes, errors, or no-ops on already-restored files.
findings.finding: The plan does not state that restore_deleted_sources / rebuild_with_restore is idempotent and resumable when interrupted mid-population or re-run across the ~505-ticket store: re-writing a `.retired` source that a prior run already restored, or re-running the rebuild, is not specified as a safe no-op.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria: 'restore_deleted_sources ... written back as a folded .retired source' and 'Restoration is per ticket ... usable on a large store'
scenarios: fsck --repair is interrupted after restoring 200 of 505 tickets and is re-run
the same ticket's restore path runs twice and re-writes an already-present .retired file
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'Restoration is idempotent — a `.retired` target that already exists is skipped, and rebuild_with_restore is re-runnable so an interrupted repair across the population can be safely resumed without double-applying.'
